title: Dubai Crown Prince Visits Injured Indian Pilot Smit Machchhar in Hospital
excerpt: Sheikh Hamdan praised flydubai captain Smit Machchhar for 'the highest degrees of courage' after the FZ1073 cockpit attack, as UAE prosecutors said the co-pilot had attempted a terrorist act.
body:
• On Saturday, Dubai Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed visited Captain Smit Machchhar in hospital, praising the Indian pilot for embodying "the highest degrees of courage, responsibility, and care for human life" during the September 30 flydubai FZ1073 cockpit attack.
  • The Crown Prince, who is also the UAE's Defence Minister, shared photographs of the visit on social media, saying the UAE's leadership had given the 39-year-old pilot its "full appreciation and praise".
  • UAE Attorney-General Dr. Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said on the same day that investigators found the co-pilot had attempted "a terrorist act", the first official terrorism framing of the incident; flydubai has temporarily suspended Tel Aviv flights at the authorities' request.
  • Mid-flight over Saudi Arabia at 34,000 feet on September 30, the co-pilot attacked Machchhar in the cockpit and the aircraft plunged more than 17,000 feet before the captain fought back, opened the locked cockpit door and diverted safely to Tabuk; all aboard were accounted for.

The Visit

Dubai Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum visited Captain Smit Machchhar in hospital on Saturday, October 3, sharing photographs of the meeting on social media. The Crown Prince — who also serves as the UAE's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence — praised the flydubai pilot in the highest terms.

https://x.com/Outlookindia/status/2106572532467769624

"The flydubai pilot who embodied the highest degrees of courage, responsibility, and care for human life. From us, and from the leadership of the nation, he has our full appreciation and praise. We are proud that he is part of our team… part of the story of our nation… and part of what the UAE stands for… a nation of compassion… a nation of peace… and a nation of life."

— Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, on X

No formal award was announced — but the visit, the public photographs and the explicit praise from the UAE leadership amount to a state-level recognition of the Indian pilot's actions.

Terrorism Framing and Investigation

On the same day, the UAE's Attorney-General, Dr. Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said investigations had revealed that the co-pilot had attempted to carry out a terrorist act, and that a specialised Public Prosecution team had been formed to investigate. It is the first official framing of the incident as terrorism.

The UAE's General Civil Aviation Authority separately praised the captain, the crew and the passengers for their response. flydubai has temporarily suspended its Tel Aviv flights at the request of authorities.

What Happened on FZ1073

Flight FZ1073, a flydubai service from Dubai International Airport to Tel Aviv carrying around 180 people, was cruising at about 34,000 feet over Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, September 30, when the co-pilot attacked Captain Machchhar inside the cockpit.

The aircraft plunged more than 17,000 feet. Despite serious injuries and massive blood loss, Machchhar fought back and managed to open the locked cockpit door, at which point passengers and crew rushed in and restrained the attacker. On-duty flydubai crew travelling as passengers on the flight helped secure the aircraft, which was diverted to Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia and landed safely. All aboard were accounted for.

One passenger, dentist Shota Musaev, told CNN that Machchhar had suffered massive blood loss and that a few more moments' delay could have cost him his life.

The Pilot

Machchhar, 39, is a father of two with 17 years of flying experience. He has been transferred to Abu Dhabi and is recovering well, with the Indian Embassy in the UAE coordinating with his family and thanking the UAE government for its care.

In a televised video call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Machchhar said: "I was fighting for my life," adding that he could tell what was happening to the plane "even with my eyes closed." Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had earlier called him a "true hero" who prevented a 9/11-scale disaster, and US President Donald Trump also weighed in with praise.

Diaspora Angle

The UAE's top leadership publicly adopting a 39-year-old Indian pilot as "part of the story of our nation" is among the strongest signals yet of how much the Gulf's roughly 4-million-strong Indian diaspora matters to the Emirates. For Indian families across the UAE and beyond, Machchhar's story has become a symbol of quiet professionalism recognised at the highest level.
